A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EAC study. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and complete appendices support comparison, including material relocated or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original forecasting experiments across three datasets, backbone comparisons, efficiency measurements and prompt-pool analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and additionally reports yearly forecasting results and a frequency-domain analysis of PEMS-Stream data.

M1.justification: The node-level prompt pool, expansion for new nodes, low-rank factorization, initial joint training and subsequent frozen-backbone tuning are unchanged. The revised Section 4 overview and Figure 2 clarify the existing procedure; Algorithm 1 is retained.

E1.justification: Both versions use Air-Stream, PEMS-Stream and Energy-Stream with the same periods and expanding-node forecasting tasks, including the same few-shot scenario. The new appendix analyzes existing PEMS-Stream coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds an ST-CRL comparison in Table 6 using scores attributed to its original paper, without reporting a rerun. Existing comparators remain; Online-ST is renamed Continual-ST. Other methods discussed as unsuitable are not added to numerical comparisons.

E3.justification: New Appendix D introduces Fourier transformation and high-frequency energy ratios for analyzing noise across periods. Existing forecasting splits, prediction horizons, metrics, model configurations and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix D and Figure 8 add a diagnostic analysis of whether frequency-domain noise characteristics help explain yearly performance variation, particularly in 2014 and 2017. Existing few-shot, backbone, rank-sensitivity and efficiency analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five repetitions and report means and standard deviations. Table 8 follows that existing practice; v2 introduces no changed run count, explicit seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 adds cited ST-CRL scores in Table 6, yearly Retrain-ST and EAC scores in Table 8, and frequency distributions in Figure 8. Tables 1–4 retain their numerical results. Table 8's averages reproduce existing aggregate results, including EAC's PEMS-Stream MAE of 13.53.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1 corrects normalization from 1/n to 1/n^2 in Equations 3 and 5 and adjusts corresponding factors in Equations 7 and 10, matching Section 4.1's definition. The propositions and low-rank proof otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same expand/compress contributions and claims of effectiveness, efficiency, simplicity, universality and lightweight tuning. Additional evidence does not redefine these central claims.

C2.justification: New discussion attributes error differences to spatial dependencies, turbine shutdowns and yearly noise characteristics. Appendix F.1 expands arguments about parameter growth, storage and historical-data privacy. The original limitations concerning graph contraction, time span and parameter inflation are retained.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a code repository address and states availability, replacing v1's future-release promise. Appendix F.1 also reports model-versus-data storage sizes. Existing hardware, hyperparameters and implementation settings remain unchanged; repository availability was not externally verified.

R1.justification: v2 adds Yi et al. (2024), identified as CMuST, and expands Appendix C.2 with comparison-suitability arguments concerning ST-CRL, URCL, UniST, FlashST and CMuST. The main related-work framing remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the methodology overview, renames Online-ST to Continual-ST, adds acknowledgments and inserts appendix results and discussion sections. Existing STGNN details and limitations are retained under new appendix numbering; most prose and the main section sequence remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 6 and 8 and Figure 8, redraws Figure 2 to make node prompts more explicit, and updates baseline labels in existing displays. The hyperparameter table is renumbered, with limited resizing and reflow elsewhere.

improvement.justification: Corrected proof normalization, explicit code-access information and yearly results improve consistency and transparency. The noise analysis adds useful diagnostic evidence without changing the main findings. These gains are limited: the ST-CRL comparison uses cited scores, and Appendix F.1 overstates standard EAC's Air-Stream speed, since Figure 6 reports 96 seconds versus STKEC's 93 seconds. Overall, the revision provides a modest quality improvement.
